title: o-mcp/subgraph version 1
description: Part of a plant's energy and water network as of one date: a root node, everything below it down to a depth, and the parents that feed into that part from outside it. Edges point the way energy or water flows. Only rows in effect on query.as_of are included. Explained further in design/subgraph-format.md. Unknown fields may appear in later version-1 documents; ignore them.

schema.description: Names the format. Check it, and version, before reading anything else.

version.description: Format version. Adding fields keeps it at 1; removing, renaming or changing the meaning of a field makes 2.

root.description: The node code asked for. If no node with this code is in effect on as_of, nodes is empty.

as_of.description: The day the plant is described as of, YYYY-MM-DD.

depth.description: How many levels below the root were followed.

utility.description: When set, only edges of this utility (ELECTRICITY, WATER, AIR, GAS, STEAM) were followed and returned. Null means all utilities.

nodes.description: Every node in the document, each once. Ordered by scope (reached, parent, context), then depth, then code.

code.description: The node's code, unique within the tenant. Edges and findings refer to nodes by this code.

name.description: Human-readable name, as the site calls it.

class.description: Broad role. SOURCE: brings energy or water in (grid incomer, PV plant, generator, well). BUS: a point where flow is shared out (switchboard, header); a main board and a sub-board are both BUS, told apart by type (MAIN_LV_BOARD, SUB_BOARD). CONVERSION: takes energy in one utility and delivers a different one (an air compressor takes electricity and delivers compressed air; a boiler, steam). TREATMENT: the same utility passes through, changed in quality and with some lost (clarifier, softener, RO unit, air dryer); inflow minus outflow is a real loss, and any electricity it draws is auxiliary. STORAGE: holds or compensates (tank, capacitor bank). LOAD: consumes.

type.description: Specific node type from the ontology, such as MAIN_LV_BOARD, PV_PLANT or AIR_COMPRESSOR. Null if not yet typed.

attrs.description: The node's recorded properties. A missing key means not recorded; that is a problem only if a PROPERTY_GAP finding names it. The unit is in the key: nominal_v and tx_primary_v in volts, rated_kva in kVA, rated_kw in kW, rated_kvar in kvar, main_breaker_a in amperes. On a board fed by a transformer, rated_kva, tx_primary_v and tx_equipment_code describe that transformer.

scope.description: Why the node is here. reached: part of the asked-for section, found walking down from the root. parent: not part of it, but feeds a reached node from outside (a second board, a PV plant, a generator). context: feeds a parent node; present only so that edge has both ends.

depth.description: For reached nodes, the fewest edges from the root (the root is 0; a node reachable two ways gets the shorter). Not a voltage level or a rank. Null for parent and context nodes.

children_total.description: How many nodes this node feeds, in or out of the document.

children_not_included.description: Of those, how many are not in the document. Above zero means the section stops here; it does not mean the node feeds nothing.

edges.description: Every edge into a reached or parent node, so each reached node's full set of parents is present. Both ends of every edge are in nodes. Ordered by from, to, id.

from.description: Code of the node the flow comes from.

to.description: Code of the node the flow goes to.

type.description: Specific edge type from the ontology, such as TRANSFORMER (a 20/0.4 kV transformer between the two nodes), SUPPLY_LV (a low-voltage feeder), PV_INJECTION or PF_COMPENSATION. Null if not yet typed.

class.description: Broad edge class, the conveyance. FEEDER: an electrical connection (what kind is in type). PIPE: a pipe carrying the utility. COMPENSATION: a capacitor bank's connection, which moves no energy.

utility.description: What flows along it: ELECTRICITY, WATER, AIR, GAS or STEAM.

carries_flow.description: False for a connection that moves no energy or water, such as a capacitor bank on a board. Do not add such edges into flow totals.

effective_from.description: When this edge became true, YYYY-MM-DD, or "-infinity" for since before records began.

effective_to.description: Last day this edge is true, YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it still is.

findings.description: What the server noticed about these nodes and edges. Computed by the server; display them, do not work them out again. Each has a code and a message to show a person as is. Ordered by code, then subject.

oneOf.description: A reached node with more than one live parent that is not a source. The plant may have only one: this is an open question for the site, not a fact.
A node that is not a bus but feeds more than one node, so the busbar they share on site has no node of its own. Expected where a site has one incomer.

children.description: How many nodes it feeds directly, counting only edges that carry flow.

oneOf.description: A property that a named reader needs and the node does not have, from graph.v_property_gaps. A property that is merely absent and not needed is not a gap. Judged on current values, so it does not change with as_of.

property.description: The missing key, as it would appear in attrs.

kind.description: Where the value would come from, such as NAMEPLATE (read off the equipment) or DESIGN.

status.description: What is wrong, such as MISSING.

used_by.description: The report or program that needs it.

detail.description: Extra detail, when there is any.

oneOf.description: An edge that breaks the edge ontology, from graph.v_edge_gaps. Judged on today's graph, so it does not change with as_of.

from.description: Code of the node it comes from.

to.description: Code of the node it goes to.

status.description: UNTYPED (no edge type), ENDPOINT_UNTYPED (an end has no node type) or ILLEGAL_ENDPOINT (its edge type does not allow these node types).
